# magic_device

> Device signals for Flutter: whether the device is on mains power (`DevicePower.charging`), whether the viewer is away (`DevicePower.idle`) and whether the macOS window is fullscreen (`WindowFullscreen`). One import, no setup, no Runner edits.

**Stack**: Flutter >=3.27.0 · Dart >=3.6.0 · Runtime deps: `battery_plus`, `flutter_inactive_timer`. `WindowFullscreen` uses the Flutter SDK only. No mocking library, no state management library.

**Setup**:

```bash
flutter pub add magic_device
```

```dart
import 'package:magic_device/magic_device.dart';

// Gate a heavy background job on mains power and an away viewer.
final DevicePower power = DevicePower(); // one owner calls start() and stop()
power.start();

if (await power.charging && power.idle) {
  // Safe to run the job.
}

power.stop();

// macOS window fullscreen state and toggle.
final WindowFullscreen fullscreen = WindowFullscreen.instance;

if (fullscreen.available) {
  await fullscreen.toggle();
}
```

Nothing is collected until `start()`; `stop()` resets `idle` to false.

## API

- `DevicePower`: `charging` (async, on mains power: `full`, `charging` and `connectedNotCharging` count; `discharging`, `unknown` and a platform without a battery implementation do not), `idle` (sync, cached after `start()`: on native macOS and Windows no input for `idleThreshold`, 2 minutes; everywhere else any app lifecycle state but `resumed`, immediately and with no threshold), `start()`, `stop()`. Constructor readers for tests: `batteryState`, `idleDuration`, `platform`, `television`.
- `WindowFullscreen`: `available` (true on macOS only), `active` (as the window last confirmed), `target` (moves on AppKit's will-notification), `transitioning`, `toggle()`, `pressTimeout` (1 second), `resetInstance()` for tests. It is a `ChangeNotifier`: add and remove a listener, never dispose the shared instance.
- `BatteryState`: re-exported from `battery_plus` so a custom `batteryState` reader names the type without a direct dependency.

## Platforms

- `DevicePower` is plain Dart over `battery_plus` with no native code of its own. System-wide idle (last input clock) works on macOS and Windows only; every other platform reports idle whenever the app is not in front, from the app lifecycle.
- `WindowFullscreen` is macOS only. The package ships its own macOS plugin (`MagicDevicePlugin`, channel `magic_device/window`), so the host's `MainFlutterWindow.swift` stays Flutter's stock one. Everywhere else `toggle()` sends nothing and `available` is false.

## Rules for agents

- Import only `package:magic_device/magic_device.dart`; everything under `src/` is private.
- Use `DevicePower.instance`, or build one `DevicePower(...)` when you must inject a reader. Let one component own `start()` and `stop()`: `stop()` has no reference count and resets `idle` to false for every consumer.
- To fake or replace the battery read, pass `batteryState:` instead of calling `Battery()` yourself.
- Pass `television: () => isTelevision` on Android TV: a batteryless TV reports `unknown`, which would read as not charging forever.
- Use `WindowFullscreen.instance` and gate every control on `available`. `toggle()` throws a `PlatformException` (`no_window`) when the Flutter view is not in a window.
- In tests, inject the readers and call `WindowFullscreen.resetInstance()` in `tearDown`. The app lifecycle is the one read that cannot be injected; drive it through the test binding.

- [DevicePower](https://anilcancakir.com/magic_device/docs/basics/device-power.md): charging and idle in depth, televisions, lifecycle ownership, gotchas.
